To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we did not find any CDKN2A mutations in patients with early-onset cancers, and that the most frequent CDKN2A variants in our patients were A148T and intron 3+29 g>c.
CDKN2A and ARF mutations are not a major cause of familial breast cancer, familial melanoma or pancreatic cancer in the Polish population.
we have found that CDKN2A gene does not contribute to the development of early onset breast cancer, pancreatic and malignant melanoma among Polish population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CDKN2 gene mutations in the etiopathogenesis of early-onset cancer of the breast, melanoma and pancreas in the Polish population.
the role of CDKN2a/ARF in the development of early-onset breast, pancreatic and melanoma cancers.
the role of the p16/INK4a/ARF tumor suppressor gene in the development of breast, pancreatic and malignant melanoma cancers in Poland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in Poland the role of CDKN2 mutations in breast cancer, pancreatic and melanoma is not as significant as in other populations.
the CDKN2A gene does not play a significant role in the development of early-onset cancers in Polish population.

the CDKN2A gene is not a high-penetrance susceptibility gene in Polish families with early-onset cancers, and the contribution of CDK2A/ARFs to the development of early-onset cancers in the Polish population is negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDKN2A mutations are rare and not a common cause of early-onset breast, pancreas, and melanoma cancer in the Polish population.
the CDKN2A gene has no role in the development of early-onset breast, pancreatic and melanoma in the Polish population.
CDKN2A is an important gene, but it is not the most important gene in melanoma, and it is not the only gene that contributes to the familial clustering of melanoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the prevalence of CDKN 2A mutations is lower among patients with early-onset cancers in Poland than in the USA and Australia, which may suggest that the role of CDKN 1A mutations is different in these populations.
in the Polish patients with early-onset cancers the role of CDKN2/ARF is limited.
the CDKN2A gene is not a major contributor to familial pancreatic cancer in the Polish population.
